cards.name: Tupolev Tu-204
cards.subtitle: Aviastar-SP · first flew 1989
cards.description: The Tupolev Tu-204 (Russian: Туполев Ту-204) is a twin-engined medium-range narrow-body jet airliner capable of carrying 210 passengers, designed by Tupolev and produced by Aviastar-SP and Kazan Aircraft Production Association. First introduced in 1995, it was intended to be broadly equivalent to the Boeing 757, with slightly lower range and payload, and had competitive performance and fuel efficiency in its class.
cards.keyFeatures: The Tu-204 was designed as a family of aircraft incorporating passenger, cargo, combi and quick-change variants. It is powered by either two Aviadvigatel PS-90 or Rolls-Royce RB211 engines.
cards.imageCredit: Juergen Lehle, CC BY-SA 3.0 via Wikimedia Commons

cards.name: Basler BT-67
cards.subtitle: first flew 1990
cards.description: The Basler BT-67 is a utility aircraft produced by Basler Turbo Conversions of Oshkosh, Wisconsin. It is a remanufactured and modified airframe of the Douglas C-47 Skytrain or the Douglas DC-3; the modifications are designed to significantly extend the DC-3's serviceable lifetime.
cards.keyFeatures: Basler Turbo Conversions was founded in 1990 solely to convert existing C-47 and DC-3 airframes into BT-67s. Basler configures each conversion to a client's specifications.
cards.imageCredit: RuthAS, CC BY 3.0 via Wikimedia Commons

cards.name: Ilyushin Il-114
cards.subtitle: Russian Aircraft Corporation MiG · first flew 1990
cards.description: The Ilyushin Il-114 (Russian Илью́шин Ил-114) is a twin-engine turboprop, short-haul regional airliner developed by the Ilyushin design bureau. The programme was launched in June 1986 by the Soviet Ministry of Aviation Industry and first flew on 29 March 1990. Initial plans envisioned the production of up to one-hundred aircraft per year, taking place in the Uzbek SSR.
cards.keyFeatures: In June 1986, the Ilyushin OKB began work on a replacement for the Antonov An-24, large numbers of which remained in service with Aeroflot.
cards.imageCredit: Public domain via Wikimedia Commons

cards.name: Learjet 60
cards.subtitle: Bombardier Aerospace · first flew 1990
cards.description: The Learjet 60 is a mid-size cabin, medium-range business jet aircraft that was manufactured by Bombardier Aerospace in Wichita, Kansas, United States. Powered by two Pratt & Whitney Canada PW305A engines, it has a range (with 4 passengers and 2 crew) of 2,405 nautical miles (4,454 km) with NBAA 100 nmi (190 km) reserves, ISA.
cards.keyFeatures: The Learjet 60 is an improved version of the Learjet 55, with a longer fuselage and more powerful turbofan engines. It first flew on 10 October 1990 and received FAA certification in January 1993.
cards.imageCredit: Lars Henseleit (Lhensele at de.wikipedia), Public domain via Wikimedia Commons

cards.name: McDonnell Douglas MD-11
cards.subtitle: Boeing · first flew 1990
cards.description: The McDonnell Douglas MD-11 is an American trijet wide-body airliner which was manufactured by McDonnell Douglas and later by Boeing. The MD-11 is the largest trijet ever built. Following DC-10 development studies, the MD-11 program was launched on December 30, 1986.
cards.keyFeatures: The MD-11 is a medium- to long-range widebody airliner, with two engines mounted on underwing pylons and a third engine at the base of the vertical stabilizer, which has a two-segment rudder for directional control.
cards.imageCredit: KLM_McDonnell_Douglas_MD-11_PH-KCK.jpg: Boushh_TFA from Kortenhoef, The Netherla, CC BY-SA 2.0 via Wikimedia Commons

cards.name: Airbus A340
cards.subtitle: Airbus Commercial Aircraft · first flew 1991
cards.description: The Airbus A340 is a long-range, wide-body passenger airliner that was developed and produced by Airbus. In the mid-1970s, Airbus conceived several derivatives of the A300, its first airliner, and developed the A340 quadjet in parallel with the A330 twinjet. In June 1987, Airbus launched both designs with their first orders, with the A340-300 taking its maiden flight on 25 October 1991.
cards.keyFeatures: The Airbus A340 is a twin-aisle passenger airliner that was the first long-range Airbus, powered by four turbofan jet engines. It was developed with technology from earlier Airbus aircraft and their features, like the A320 glass cockpit; it shares many components with the A330, notably identical fly-by-wire control systems and similar wings.
cards.imageCredit: Iberia Airlines, CC BY 2.0 via Wikimedia Commons

cards.name: British Aerospace Jetstream 41
cards.subtitle: British Aerospace · first flew 1991
cards.description: The British Aerospace Jetstream 41 is a turboprop-powered feederliner and regional airliner, designed by British Aerospace as a stretched version of the Jetstream 31. Intended to compete directly with 30-seat aircraft like the Embraer Brasilia, Dornier 328 and Saab 340, the new design eventually accommodated 29 passengers in a two-by-one arrangement like the Jetstream 31.
cards.keyFeatures: The Jetstream 41's stretch added 16 feet (4.9 m) to the fuselage, consisting of an 8-foot-3-inch (2.51 m) plug forward of the wing and a 7 feet 9 inches (2.36 m) plug to the rear; the fuselage design was all-new with no commonality with the old fuselage. The wing had increased span and redesigned ailerons and flaps.
cards.imageCredit: Adrian Pingstone (Arpingstone), Public domain via Wikimedia Commons

cards.name: Bombardier CRJ
cards.subtitle: Canadair · first flew 1991
cards.description: The Bombardier CRJ/Mitsubishi CRJ or CRJ Series (for Canadair Regional Jet) is a family of regional jets introduced in 1991 by Bombardier Aerospace. The CRJ was manufactured by Bombardier Aerospace with the manufacturing of the first CRJ generation, the CRJ100/200 starting in 1991 and the second CRJ generation, the CRJ700 series starting in 1999.
cards.imageCredit: André Gerwing, CC BY-SA 4.0 via Wikimedia Commons

cards.name: Sukhoi Su-29
cards.subtitle: Sukhoi · first flew 1991
cards.description: The Sukhoi Su-29 is a Russian two-seat aerobatic aircraft with a 268 kW (360 hp) radial engine. It was designed based on the Su-26 and inherited most of the design and technical features of its predecessor. Due to wide use of composite materials, which make up as much as 60% of the Su-29's aircraft structure, the empty weight is increased by only 50 kg (110 lb) over the single-seat Su-26's empty weight.
cards.imageCredit: Original uploader was Mottld at en.wikipedia, Public domain via Wikimedia Commons

cards.name: Airbus A330
cards.subtitle: Airbus Commercial Aircraft · first flew 1992
cards.description: The Airbus A330 is a wide-body airliner developed and produced by Airbus. Airbus began developing larger A300 derivatives in the mid–1970s, giving rise to the A330 twinjet as well as the Airbus A340 quadjet, and launched both designs along with their first orders in June 1987. The A330-300, the first variant, took its maiden flight in November 1992 and entered service with Air Inter in January 1994.
cards.keyFeatures: The A330 is a medium-size, wide-body aircraft, with two engines suspended on pylons under the wings. A two-wheel nose undercarriage and two four-wheel bogie main legs built by Messier-Dowty support the aircraft on the ground.
cards.imageCredit: Ken Fielding, CC BY-SA 3.0 via Wikimedia Commons

cards.name: Saab 2000
cards.subtitle: Saab Group · first flew 1992
cards.description: The Saab 2000 is a twin-engined high-speed turboprop airliner built by Swedish aircraft manufacturer Saab. It is designed to carry 50–58 passengers and able to cruise at a maximum speed of 685 km/h (370 kn). Production took place in Linköping, Sweden.
cards.imageCredit: ISORauscht, CC BY-SA 4.0 via Wikimedia Commons

cards.name: Airbus A321
cards.subtitle: Airbus Commercial Aircraft · first flew 1993
cards.description: The Airbus A321 is a member of the Airbus A320 family of short to medium range, narrow-body, commercial passenger twin engine jet airliners; it carries 185 to 239 passengers. It has a stretched fuselage which was the first derivative of the baseline A320 and entered service in 1994, about six years after the original A320.
cards.keyFeatures: The Airbus A321 is a narrow-body (single-aisle) aircraft with a retractable tricycle landing gear, powered by two wing pylon-mounted turbofan engines. It is a low-wing cantilever monoplane with a conventional tail unit having a single vertical stabilizer and rudder.
cards.imageCredit: Arpingstone, Public domain via Wikimedia Commons

cards.name: Canadair CL-415
cards.subtitle: Canadair · first flew 1993
cards.description: The Canadair CL-415 (Super Scooper, later Bombardier 415) and the De Havilland Canadair DHC-515 are a series of amphibious aircraft built originally by Canadair and subsequently by Bombardier and De Havilland Canada. The CL-415 is based on the Canadair CL-215 and is designed specifically for aerial firefighting, although it can perform various other roles, such as search and rescue and utility transport.
cards.keyFeatures: The CL-415 has an updated cockpit, aerodynamics enhancements, and changes to the water-release system creating a modern firefighting amphibious flying boat for use in detecting and suppressing forest fires. Compared to the CL-215, the CL-415 has increased operating weight and speed, yielding improved productivity and performance.
cards.imageCredit: Maarten Visser from Capelle aan den IJssel, Nederland, CC BY-SA 2.0 via Wikimedia Commons

cards.name: Dassault Falcon 2000
cards.subtitle: Dassault Aviation · first flew 1993
cards.description: The Dassault Falcon 2000 is a business jet produced in France by Dassault Aviation, a member of its Falcon business jet line. Developed from the Falcon 900 trijet, the smaller twinjet has less range.
cards.keyFeatures: The Falcon 900 fuselage was shortened by 7 ft (2.1 m) to carry up to 10 passengers. The wing leading edge was modified and its inboard slats were removed.
cards.imageCredit: Adrian Pingstone, Public domain via Wikimedia Commons

cards.name: Fokker 70
cards.subtitle: Fokker · first flew 1993
cards.description: The Fokker 70 is a narrow-body, twin-engined, medium-range, turbofan regional airliner designed and produced by the now defunct Dutch aircraft manufacturer Fokker. It was developed during the early 1990s as a smaller version of the newly-developed Fokker 100. Both the Fokker 70 and Fokker 100 were preceded by the first jet airliner manufactured by the company, the Fokker F28 Fellowship.
cards.keyFeatures: The Fokker 70 is a narrow-body, twin-engined, medium-range regional airliner. It is powered by a pair of Rolls-Royce Tay 620 turbofan engines, positioned at either side of the aircraft and mounted on the rear fuselage; each engine is capable of providing up to 61.6 kN (13,849 lb) of thrust.
cards.imageCredit: Arpingstone, Public domain via Wikimedia Commons

cards.name: PZL M28 Skytruck
cards.subtitle: PZL Mielec · first flew 1993
cards.description: The PZL M28 Skytruck is a family of Polish light utility aircraft with STOL capability produced by PZL Mielec for military and civilian use. They are mainly used in transport, patrol and maritime reconnaissance roles. The maritime patrol and reconnaissance variants are designated PZL M28B Bryza (English: Breeze), while variant in the U.S.
cards.keyFeatures: The M28 is a twin-engined high-wing strutted monoplane with an all-metal airframe, twin vertical fins and a tricycle fixed landing gear. If an engine fails, a spoiler forward of the aileron opens automatically on the opposite wing.
cards.imageCredit: Airwolfhound from Hertfordshire, UK, CC BY-SA 2.0 via Wikimedia Commons

cards.name: Airbus Beluga
cards.subtitle: Airbus Commercial Aircraft · first flew 1994
cards.description: The Airbus A300-600ST (Super Transporter) or Beluga is a specialised wide-body airliner used to transport aircraft parts and outsize cargoes. It received the official name of Super Transporter early on, but its nickname, after the beluga whale, which it resembles, gained popularity and has since been officially adopted.
cards.keyFeatures: The A300-600ST Beluga shares many design similarities, although differing substantially in appearance, to the Airbus A300 upon which it was based.
cards.imageCredit: Brian Bukowski, CC BY-SA 2.0 via Wikimedia Commons

cards.name: Antonov An-38
cards.subtitle: Novosibirsk Aircraft Production Association · first flew 1994
cards.description: The Antonov An-38 is a stretched and upgraded version of Antonov's earlier An-28. It is a twin-engined turboprop transport aircraft, designed by the Antonov Design Bureau in Kyiv, Ukraine. Production is in Novosibirsk, Russia, but some crucial parts are also made in Ukraine and Belarus.
cards.keyFeatures: Impetus for a stretch of the Antonov An-28 design began with a 1989 sales tour in India, where it became clear that a significant market existed for an aircraft similar to the An-28, but with seating in the 25–30 seat range. The design was approved a year later, and was displayed at the 1991 Paris Air Show as a model.
cards.imageCredit: Gleb Osokin - Russian AviaPhoto Team, CC BY-SA 3.0 via Wikimedia Commons

cards.name: Boeing 777
cards.subtitle: Boeing Commercial Airplanes · first flew 1994
cards.description: The Boeing 777, commonly referred to as the Triple Seven, is an American long-range wide-body airliner developed and manufactured by Boeing Commercial Airplanes. The 777 is the world's largest twinjet and the most-built wide-body airliner. The jetliner was designed to bridge the gap between Boeing's other wide body airplanes, the twin-engined 767 and quad-engined 747, and to replace aging DC-10 and L-1011 trijets.
cards.keyFeatures: Boeing introduced a number of advanced technologies with the 777 design, including fully digital fly-by-wire controls, fully software-configurable avionics, LCD glass cockpit flight displays from Honeywell, and the first use of a fiber optic avionics network on a commercial airliner.
cards.imageCredit: CC BY-SA 2.0 via Wikimedia Commons

cards.name: Ilyushin Il-103
cards.subtitle: Ilyushin · first flew 1994
cards.description: The Ilyushin Il-103 is a single-engine, low-wing training aircraft developed by the Ilyushin Design Bureau that started in 1990 in the Soviet Union. The aircraft is now produced in Russia. It was the first Russian aircraft to achieve Federal Aviation Administration certification in 1998, it is for sale in the United States.
cards.imageCredit: CC BY 2.5 via Wikimedia Commons

cards.name: Airbus A319
cards.subtitle: Airbus Commercial Aircraft · first flew 1995
cards.description: The Airbus A319 is a member of the Airbus A320 family of short- to medium-range, narrow-body, commercial passenger twin-engine jet airliners manufactured by Airbus. The A319 carries 124 to 156 passengers and has a maximum range of 3,700 nmi (6,900 km; 4,300 mi). Final assembly of the aircraft took place in Hamburg, Germany and Tianjin, China.
cards.imageCredit: Anna Zvereva from Tallinn, Estonia, CC BY-SA 2.0 via Wikimedia Commons

cards.name: Cirrus SR20
cards.subtitle: Cirrus Aircraft Corporation · first flew 1995
cards.description: The Cirrus SR20 is an American piston-engined, four- or five-seat composite monoplane built since 1999 by Cirrus Aircraft of Duluth, Minnesota. The aircraft is the company's earliest type-certified model, earning certification in 1998.
cards.keyFeatures: The SR20 mock-up was unveiled in 1994. The aircraft first flew on 21 March 1995 and FAA certification was achieved on 23 October 1998.
cards.imageCredit: Tomás Del Coro from Las Vegas, Nevada, USA, CC BY-SA 2.0 via Wikimedia Commons

cards.name: Embraer ERJ family
cards.subtitle: Embraer · first flew 1995
cards.description: The Embraer ERJ family (for Embraer Regional Jet) are regional jets designed and produced by the Brazilian aerospace company Embraer. The family includes the ERJ 135 (37 passengers), ERJ 140 (44 passengers), and ERJ 145 (50 passengers), as well as the Legacy 600 business jet and the R-99 family of military aircraft. Development of the ERJ 145 was launched in 1989.
cards.keyFeatures: The Embraer ERJ family is a series of twin-engine regional jets. The ERJ family retains a relatively high level of commonality with the Embraer Legacy 600 business jet; the principal difference being the addition of winglets and additional fuel tanks as standard on the latter.
cards.imageCredit: Adrian Pingstone, Public domain via Wikimedia Commons

cards.name: Gulfstream V
cards.subtitle: Gulfstream Aerospace · first flew 1995
cards.description: The Gulfstream V is a large, long-range business jet aircraft produced by Gulfstream Aerospace, derived from the previous Gulfstream IV. It has a maximum speed of Mach 0.885 (584 mph; 508 kn; 940 km/h), flight ceiling of 51,000 feet (16,000 m), and a maximum range of 6,500 nmi (7,500 mi; 12,000 km). It typically accommodates four crew and 14 passengers.
cards.keyFeatures: The engines are now Rolls-Royce BR700-710A1-10 with increased thrust, a higher bypass ratio, and Full Authority Digital Engine Controls (FADEC). Operating ceiling increased from 45,000 to 51,000 ft (14,000 to 16,000 m).
cards.imageCredit: Alan Radecki Akradecki, CC BY-SA 3.0 via Wikimedia Commons

cards.name: Myasishchev M-101T
cards.subtitle: Sokol · first flew 1995
cards.description: The Myasishchev M-101T is a Russian business class aircraft, designed by Myasishchev and built by Sokol. The aircraft was first flown on 31 March 1995.
cards.imageCredit: Jozef Tóth, CC BY-SA 3.0 via Wikimedia Commons

cards.name: Bombardier Global Express
cards.subtitle: Bombardier · first flew 1996
cards.description: The Bombardier Global Express is a large cabin, long-range business jet designed and manufactured by Bombardier Aviation. Announced in October 1991, it first flew in October 1996, received its Canadian type certification in July 1998 and entered service in July 1999.
cards.keyFeatures: The Global Express is a high speed business/corporate aircraft with a range of 6,500 nmi (7,500 mi; 12,000 km) at Mach 0.80 (528 mph; 459 kn; 850 km/h), a 51,000 ft (16,000 m) service ceiling and a 14-hour endurance. The semi monocoque airframe is made of lightweight aluminum alloys and composite materials.
cards.imageCredit:
Wo st 01
(There are 682 Pictures in my Category)

See also Toolserver, CC BY-SA 3.0 de via Wikimedia Commons

cards.name: Antonov An-140
cards.subtitle: KhAZ · first flew 1997
cards.description: The Antonov An-140 is a turboprop regional airliner, designed by the Ukrainian Antonov ASTC bureau as a successor to the Antonov An-24, with extended cargo capacity and the ability to use unprepared airstrips.
cards.keyFeatures: First flown on 17 September 1997, the 52 passenger An-140 is manufactured at the main production line in Kharkiv by KHDABP, in Samara by Aviakor, and assembled under license by Iran Aircraft Manufacturing Industrial Company (HESA) in Iran as the IrAn-140.
cards.imageCredit: Dmitry A. Mottl, CC BY-SA 3.0 via Wikimedia Commons

cards.name: Boeing 737 Next Generation
cards.subtitle: Boeing Commercial Airplanes · first flew 1997
cards.description: The Boeing 737 Next Generation, commonly abbreviated as 737NG, or 737 Next Gen, is a twin-engined narrow-body aircraft produced by Boeing Commercial Airplanes. Launched in 1993 as the third-generation derivative of the Boeing 737, it has been produced since 1997. The 737NG is an upgrade of the 737 Classic series.
cards.keyFeatures: The wing was redesigned with a new, thinner airfoil section, and a greater chord and increased wingspan (by 16 ft [4.9 m]) increased the wing area by 25%, which also increased total fuel capacity by 30%. New quieter and more fuel-efficient CFM56-7B engines are used.
cards.imageCredit: Brorsson, CC BY-SA 3.0 via Wikimedia Commons

cards.name: Diamond DA40 Diamond Star
cards.subtitle: Diamond Aircraft Industries · first flew 1997
cards.description: The Diamond DA40 Diamond Star is an Austrian four-seat, single-engine, light aircraft constructed from composite materials. Built in both Austria and Canada, it was developed as a four-seat version of the earlier DA20 by Diamond Aircraft Industries. By the end of December 2020, 2,200 DA40s had been delivered, including 500 NG models.
cards.keyFeatures: The DA40 is a four-seat low-wing cantilever monoplane made from composite materials. It has a fixed tricycle landing gear and a T-tail.
cards.imageCredit: Ahunt at English Wikipedia, Public domain via Wikimedia Commons

cards.name: Gulfstream G200
cards.subtitle: Gulfstream Aerospace · first flew 1997
cards.description: The Gulfstream G200, formerly known as the IAI Galaxy, is a twin-engine business jet. It was designed originally by Israel Aerospace Industries (IAI) and was produced by IAI for Gulfstream Aerospace from 1999 through 2011.
cards.keyFeatures: The G200 was originally named "Astra Galaxy". When Gulfstream Aerospace purchased Galaxy Aerospace in 2001 the model was rebranded as the Gulfstream G200.
cards.imageCredit: Captain Yen Chun, Public domain via Wikimedia Commons

cards.name: Fairchild Dornier 328JET
cards.subtitle: Dornier · first flew 1998
cards.description: The Fairchild-Dornier 328JET is a commuter airliner, based upon the turboprop-powered Dornier 328, developed by the German aircraft manufacturer Dornier Luftfahrt GmbH. It would be the last Dornier-designed aircraft to reach production before the company's collapse during the early 2000s.
cards.imageCredit: Juergen Lehle, CC BY-SA 3.0 via Wikimedia Commons

cards.name: Bombardier CRJ700 series
cards.subtitle: Bombardier Aerospace · first flew 1999
cards.description: The Bombardier CRJ700 series is a family of regional jet airliners that were designed and manufactured by Canadian transportation conglomerate Bombardier. Officially launched in 1997, the CRJ700 made its maiden flight on 27 May 1999 and was soon followed by the stretched CRJ900 variant.
cards.imageCredit: Bene Riobó, CC BY-SA 3.0 via Wikimedia Commons

cards.name: Tupolev Tu-334
cards.subtitle: Kazan Aircraft Production Association · first flew 1999
cards.description: The Tupolev Tu-334 (Russian: Туполев Ту-334) was a Russian short-to-medium range airliner project that was developed to replace the aging Tupolev Tu-134 and Yak-42s in service around the world. The airframe was based on a shortened Tu-204 fuselage and a scaled-down version of that aircraft's wing.
cards.keyFeatures: The Tupolev Design Bureau introduced the Tu-334 in early 1989 as an eventual propfan-powered airliner to potentially enter service for Aeroflot in 1995. However, it would have an interim turbofan-powered version that would begin airline service around 1991–1992.
cards.imageCredit: Зимин Василий, Public domain via Wikimedia Commons

cards.name: Cessna 400
cards.subtitle: Cessna · first flew 2000
cards.description: The Cessna 400, marketed as the Cessna Corvalis, is a single-engine, fixed-gear, low-wing general aviation aircraft built from composite materials by Cessna Aircraft. The Cessna 400 was originally built by Columbia Aircraft as the Columbia 400 until December 2007. From 2013, the aircraft was built as the Cessna T240 Corvalis TTx.
cards.keyFeatures: The Cessna 400 was derived from the normally aspirated Columbia 300, which in turn was derived from the Lancair ES kit aircraft. The 400 is powered by a turbocharged Continental TSIO-550-C engine producing 310 horsepower (230 kW) at 2600 rpm.
cards.imageCredit: Jeroen Stroes Aviation Photography from Netherlands, CC BY 2.0 via Wikimedia Commons

cards.name: Xi'an MA60
cards.subtitle: Xi'an Aircraft Industrial Corporation · first flew 2000
cards.description: The Xi'an MA60 (新舟60, Xīnzhōu liùshí, "Modern Ark 60") is a turboprop-powered airliner produced by China's Xi'an Aircraft Industrial Corporation under the Aviation Industry Corporation of China (AVIC). The MA60 is a stretched version of the Xi'an Y7-200A, which was produced based on the An-24 to operate in rugged conditions with limited ground support and has short take-off and landing (STOL) capability.
cards.keyFeatures: The Xi’an MA60 is a twin-engine turboprop aircraft designed for short regional flights, including passenger and cargo transport, maritime patrol, medical evacuation, and paratrooper operations. It features a high-wing configuration that supports stable low-speed performance and ground clearance.
cards.imageCredit: byeangel from Tsingtao, China, CC BY-SA 2.0 via Wikimedia Commons

cards.name: Embraer Legacy 600
cards.subtitle: Embraer · first flew 2001
cards.description: The Embraer Legacy 600 is a business jet derivative of the Embraer ERJ family of commercial jet aircraft.
cards.keyFeatures: The Legacy 600 (market designation adopted after 2005) is based on the ERJ-135 model. It was launched in 2000 at the Farnborough Airshow as the "Legacy 2000".
cards.imageCredit: Adrian Pingstone (Arpingstone), Public domain via Wikimedia Commons

cards.name: Sukhoi Su-80
cards.subtitle: Sukhoi · first flew 2001
cards.description: The Sukhoi Su-80 (formerly known as the Sukhoi S-80) is a Russian twin-turboprop, twin-boom STOL transport aircraft.
cards.keyFeatures: The Su-80 program was supposed to start in the late 1990s, but due to lack of funds, it was postponed for several years. A prototype of the combined Freight/Passenger Su-80GP was built and its first flight was planned for early 1998, but the program was delayed again.
cards.imageCredit: RuLavan, Public domain via Wikimedia Commons

cards.name: Airbus A318
cards.subtitle: Airbus Commercial Aircraft · first flew 2002
cards.description: The Airbus A318, nicknamed the Baby Bus, is the smallest and least numerous variant airliner of the Airbus A320 family. The A318 carries 32 to 132 passengers and has a maximum range of 5,750 kilometres (3,100 nautical miles; 3,570 miles). Final assembly of the aircraft took place in Hamburg, Germany.
cards.keyFeatures: The Airbus A318 is a small commercial, narrow-body (single-aisle) aircraft with a retractable tricycle landing gear and is powered by two wing pylon-mounted turbofan engines. Two suppliers, namely CFM International with the CFM56-5B engine and Pratt & Whitney with the PW6000 engine, provide turbofan engines for the A318.
cards.imageCredit: Aero Icarus from Zürich, Switzerland, CC BY-SA 2.0 via Wikimedia Commons

cards.name: Diamond DA42 Twin Star
cards.subtitle: Diamond Aircraft Industries · first flew 2002
cards.description: The Diamond DA42 Twin Star is a four seat, twin engine, propeller-driven airplane developed and manufactured in Austria and Canada by Diamond Aircraft Industries, an Austrian subsidiary of China-based Wanfeng Aviation since 2017. It was Diamond's first twin engine design, as well as the first new European twin-engine aircraft in its category to be developed in over 25 years.
cards.keyFeatures: The Diamond DA42 Twin Star is a twin-engined low-wing cantilever monoplane, commonly used as a general aviation aircraft for touring and training purposes. It is equipped with a retractable tricycle landing gear arrangement and uses a T-tail.
cards.imageCredit: Original uploader was Ahunt at en.wikipedia, Public domain via Wikimedia Commons

cards.name: Embraer E-Jet family
cards.subtitle: Embraer · first flew 2002
cards.description: The Embraer E-Jet family is a series of four-abreast, narrow-body, short- to medium-range, twin-engined regional jet airliners designed and produced by Brazilian aerospace manufacturer Embraer. The E-Jet was designed to complement Embraer's earlier ERJ family, the company's first jet-powered regional aircraft.
cards.keyFeatures: The Embraer E-Jet family is composed of two main commercial families and a business jet variant. The smaller E170 and E175 make up the base model aircraft, while the E190 and E195 are stretched versions, being powered by different engines and furnished with larger wing, horizontal stabilizer, and landing gear structures.
cards.imageCredit: Bene Riobó, CC BY-SA 4.0 via Wikimedia Commons

cards.name: Gulfstream G550
cards.subtitle: Gulfstream Aerospace · first flew 2002
cards.description: The Gulfstream G550 is an American business jet aircraft produced by the General Dynamics' Gulfstream Aerospace unit in Savannah, Georgia, US. The certification designation is GV-SP. A version with reduced fuel capacity was marketed as the G500.
cards.keyFeatures: Compared to the Gulfstream V, drag reduction details boost range by 250 nmi (460 km) and increase fuel efficiency. Maximum takeoff weight (MTOW) is increased by 500 lb (230 kg) and takeoff performance is enhanced.
cards.imageCredit:
Wo st 01
(There are 682 Pictures in my Category)

See also Toolserver, CC BY-SA 3.0 de via Wikimedia Commons

cards.name: Learjet 40
cards.subtitle: Bombardier Aerospace · first flew 2002
cards.description: The Learjet 40 (LJ40) is a light business jet produced by Bombardier Aerospace.
cards.keyFeatures: The Learjet 40 is derived from the Learjet 45, but with a shorter fuselage (by 24.5 inches/60 cm), and is powered by two Honeywell TFE731-20AR engines. These are known as the "AR" engines.
cards.imageCredit: scott wright, CC BY-SA 2.0 via Wikimedia Commons

cards.name: ShinMaywa US-2
cards.subtitle: ShinMaywa · first flew 2003
cards.description: The ShinMaywa US-2 is a large Japanese short takeoff and landing turboprop amphibious aircraft that employs boundary layer control technology for enhanced STOL and stall suppression performance. Manufactured by seaplane specialist ShinMaywa (formerly Shin Meiwa), it was developed from the earlier Shin Meiwa US-1A seaplane, which was introduced in the 1970s.
cards.keyFeatures: In 1969, the Japan Maritime Self-Defense Force (JMSDF) issued a production order to Japanese seaplane manufacturer Shin Meiwa for a group of 21 anti-submarine aircraft, which were given the designation PS-1. The service also procured a variant of the type, designated US-1A, specifically for search-and-rescue (SAR).
cards.imageCredit: Naokijp, CC BY-SA 4.0 via Wikimedia Commons

cards.name: Antonov An-148
cards.subtitle: Voronezh Aircraft Production Association · first flew 2004
cards.description: The Antonov An-148 (Ukrainian: Антонов Ан-148) is a regional jet designed and primarily built by the Ukrainian aerospace manufacturer Antonov of Ukraine.
cards.keyFeatures: The Antonov An-148 is a high-wing monoplane that is powered by a pair of turbofan engines that are mounted in pods under the wing. This arrangement protects the engines and wing structure against foreign object damage.
cards.imageCredit: Dmitry A. Mottl, Public domain via Wikimedia Commons

cards.name: Airbus A380
cards.subtitle: Airbus Commercial Aircraft · first flew 2005
cards.description: The Airbus A380 is a large wide-body airliner, developed and produced by Airbus from 2003 to 2021. It is the world's largest passenger airliner and the only full-length double-deck jet airliner. Airbus studies started in 1988, and the project was announced in 1990 to challenge the dominance of the Boeing 747 in the long-haul market.
cards.keyFeatures: The A380 was initially offered in two models: the A380-800 and the A380F. The A380-800's original configuration carried 555 passengers in a three-class configuration or 853 passengers (538 on the main deck and 315 on the upper deck) in a single-class economy configuration.
cards.imageCredit: Maarten Visser from Capelle aan den IJssel, Nederland, CC BY-SA 2.0 via Wikimedia Commons

cards.name: Cessna Citation Mustang
cards.subtitle: Cessna · first flew 2005
cards.description: The Cessna Citation Mustang is a very light jet that was built by Cessna. Launched at the 2002 NBAA convention, the Model 510 first flew on April 23, 2005. It received its FAA type certification on September 8, 2006, and was first delivered on November 22.
cards.keyFeatures: The Cessna Citation Mustang is a low-wing, cantilever monoplane with a tapered wing, T-tail, and retractable tricycle gear. One main door is located in the forward left section of the aircraft, with an additional emergency exit on the center right section of the fuselage.
cards.imageCredit: Juergen Lehle, CC BY 3.0 via Wikimedia Commons

cards.name: Dassault Falcon 7X
cards.subtitle: Dassault Aviation · first flew 2005
cards.description: The Dassault Falcon 7X is a large-cabin, 5,950-nautical-mile (11,019 km; 6,847 mi) range business jet manufactured by Dassault Aviation. Unveiled at the 2001 Paris Air Show, its first flight took place on 5 May 2005 and it entered service on 15 June 2007.
cards.keyFeatures: The Falcon 7X is a three-engined cantilever monoplane with a low-positioned, highly swept wing. It has a horizontal stabiliser at mid-height and a retractable tricycle landing gear, and three rear-mounted Pratt & Whitney PW307A turbofan engines: two on the sides of the fuselage and one in a center position, and room for 19 passengers and three crew.
cards.imageCredit: Dmitry A. Mottl, Public domain via Wikimedia Commons

cards.name: Boeing Dreamlifter
cards.subtitle: Evergreen Group · first flew 2006
cards.description: The Boeing Dreamlifter, officially the 747-400 Large Cargo Freighter (LCF), is an American wide-body cargo aircraft modified extensively from the Boeing 747-400 airliner. With a volume of 65,000 cubic feet (1,840 m3) it has three times the volume of a 747-400F freighter.
cards.keyFeatures: The 1960s Apollo program, in need to transport rocket sections with low weight but large diameter, had used enlarged bulging fuselage airplanes like the Super Guppy which in the 1970s were adopted by Airbus, a consortium based in several European countries that needs to transport wings and wide-body aircraft fuselage sections.
cards.imageCredit:
Boeing_747-409LCF_Dreamlifter.jpg: scott wright
derivative work: Altair78 (talk), CC BY 2.0 via Wikimedia Commons

cards.name: Embraer Phenom 100
cards.subtitle: Embraer · first flew 2007
cards.description: The Embraer EMB-500 Phenom 100 is a very light (VLJ) business jet designed and produced by the Brazilian aircraft manufacturer Embraer. Announced in November 2005, it made its first flight on 26 July 2007 and was awarded a type certificate in December 2008; the first aircraft was delivered the same month. The Phenom 100 has been stretched into the larger Embraer Phenom 300.
cards.keyFeatures: The Embraer Phenom 100 is a low wing cantilever monoplane with a T-tail and a retractable tricycle landing gear. It has an oval fuselage with a 7.985 m3 (282 ft3) passenger cabin, a 1.47 m-high by 0.74 m-wide (4.5'x2.1') door and 1.2'x1' windows.
cards.imageCredit: Greg Goebel, CC BY-SA 2.0 via Wikimedia Commons

cards.name: Comac C909
cards.subtitle: Comac · first flew 2008
cards.description: The Comac C909, originally known as the ARJ21 Xiangfeng (Chinese: 翔凤; pinyin: xiángfèng; lit. 'Soaring Phoenix'), is a 78–90 seat regional jet manufactured by the Chinese state-owned aerospace company Comac. Development of the ARJ21 began in March 2002, led by the state-owned ACAC consortium. The first prototype was rolled out on 21 December 2007, and made its maiden flight on 28 November 2008 from Shanghai.
cards.keyFeatures: Several sources have noted that the ARJ21 fuselage cross section is identical to the McDonnell Douglas MD-80 and the MD-90, which were produced under license in China. Comac states that the ARJ21 is a completely indigenous design.
cards.imageCredit: Peng Chen, CC BY-SA 2.0 via Wikimedia Commons

cards.name: Icon A5
cards.subtitle: Icon Aircraft · first flew 2008
cards.description: The Icon A5 is an American amphibious light-sport aircraft (LSA) designed and produced by Icon Aircraft. A concept aircraft was first flown in 2008, and creation of the production tooling began in December 2012. The first production aircraft made its first flight on July 7, 2014, and made its public debut at EAA AirVenture Oshkosh on July 27, 2014.
cards.keyFeatures: The A5 is a high-wing flying boat-type amphibious monoplane with a carbon fiber airframe and retractable undercarriage. It seats two people in an enclosed 46-inch-wide (116.8 cm) cockpit and is powered by a single 100 hp (75 kW) Rotax 912 iS engine driving a three-bladed pusher propeller.
cards.imageCredit: H. Michael Miley, CC BY-SA 2.0 via Wikimedia Commons

cards.name: Boeing 787 Dreamliner
cards.subtitle: Boeing Commercial Airplanes · first flew 2009
cards.description: The Boeing 787 Dreamliner, often shortened to 787, is an American wide-body airliner developed and manufactured by Boeing Commercial Airplanes. After dropping its unconventional Sonic Cruiser project, Boeing announced the conventional 7E7 on January 29, 2003, which focused largely on efficiency.
cards.keyFeatures: The Boeing 787 Dreamliner is a long-haul, widebody, twin-engine jetliner, designed with lightweight structures that are 80% composite by volume; Boeing lists its materials by weight as 50% composite, 20% aluminum, 15% titanium, 10% steel, and 5% other materials.
cards.imageCredit: Masakatsu Ukon, CC BY-SA 2.0 via Wikimedia Commons

cards.name: Gulfstream G650/G700/G800
cards.subtitle: Gulfstream Aerospace · first flew 2009
cards.description: The Gulfstream G650, G700, and G800 are large business jets produced by Gulfstream Aerospace in the United States. The G650 model is designated Gulfstream GVI in its type certificate. The aircraft can be configured to carry from 11 to 18 passengers over a range of 7,000 nautical miles [nmi] (13,000 km; 8,100 mi) at a top speed of Mach 0.925 using a new wing and improved Rolls-Royce Pearl 700 engines.
cards.keyFeatures: The G650 has a cruise speed of Mach 0.85 to 0.90, with maximum speed of Mach 0.925 and a range of up to 7,000 nautical miles [nmi] (13,000 km; 8,100 mi). It can be equipped with a full kitchen and bar as well as a variety of entertainment features including satellite phones and wireless internet.
cards.imageCredit: Waerfelu, CC BY 3.0 via Wikimedia Commons

cards.name: Boeing 747-8
cards.subtitle: Boeing Commercial Airplanes · first flew 2010
cards.description: The Boeing 747-8, as -8i intercontinental for passengers and -8F freighter, is the last member of the Boeing 747 family, a series of four-engine long-range large wide-body airliners built by Boeing Commercial Airplanes until 2023. It is the largest model of the 747 that was introduced in the 1960s, and is Boeing's largest aircraft overall.
cards.keyFeatures: The 747-8 is a development of the Boeing 747 that takes advantage of improvements in technology and aerodynamics. The two 747-8 variants feature a fuselage stretch of 18.3 ft (5.6 m) over the 747-400, bringing the total length to 250 ft 2 in (76.25 m).
cards.imageCredit: Kambui, CC BY 2.0 via Wikimedia Commons

cards.name: Airbus A350
cards.subtitle: Airbus Commercial Aircraft · first flew 2013
cards.description: The Airbus A350 is a long-range, wide-body twin-engine airliner developed and produced by Airbus. The initial A350 design, which was proposed in 2004 in response to the Boeing 787 Dreamliner, would have been a development of the Airbus A330 with composite wings, advanced winglets, and new efficient engines.
cards.keyFeatures: Airbus expected 10% lower airframe maintenance compared with the original A350 design and 14% lower empty seat weight than the Boeing 777. Design freeze for the A350-900 was achieved in December 2008.
cards.imageCredit: Adam Moreira (AEMoreira042281), CC BY-SA 4.0 via Wikimedia Commons

cards.name: Airbus A320neo family
cards.subtitle: Airbus Commercial Aircraft · first flew 2014
cards.description: The Airbus A320neo family is an incremental development of the A320 family of narrow-body airliners produced by Airbus. The A320neo family (neo being Greek for "new", as well as an acronym for "new engine option") is based on the enhanced variant of the previous generation A319, A320, and A321, which was then retroactively renamed the A320ceo family (ceo being an acronym for "current engine option").
cards.keyFeatures: In 2006 Airbus started the A320 Enhanced (A320E) programme as a series of improvements targeting a 4–5% efficiency gain with large winglets (2%), aerodynamic refinements (1%), weight savings and a new aircraft cabin.
cards.imageCredit: Pedro Aragão, CC BY-SA 3.0 via Wikimedia Commons

cards.name: Airbus A220
cards.subtitle: Airbus Canada · first flew 2015
cards.description: The Airbus A220 is a family of five-abreast narrow-body airliners by Airbus Canada Limited Partnership (ACLP). It was initially developed by Bombardier Aviation with the program launched on 13 July 2008 and had two years in-service as the Bombardier CSeries.
cards.keyFeatures: The Airbus A220 family is a five-abreast single-aisle airliner developed specifically for the 100- to 150-seat market segment between regional airliners and mainline airliners, which includes two models, the 35 m (115 ft) long A220-100 and the larger, 38.71 m (127 ft) long A220-300.
cards.imageCredit: Romain COUPY, CC BY-SA 4.0 via Wikimedia Commons

cards.name: Mitsubishi SpaceJet
cards.subtitle: MSJ Asset Management Company · first flew 2015
cards.description: The Mitsubishi SpaceJet (Japanese: 三菱スペースジェット, originally named Mitsubishi Regional Jet) was a regional jet project by Japanese company Mitsubishi Aircraft Corporation (MAC), a Mitsubishi Heavy Industries (MHI) subsidiary, that ran from 2007 to 2023.
cards.keyFeatures: In September 2009, Mitsubishi unveiled extensive design changes, using aluminium instead of carbon fibre composites for the aircraft's wings and wingbox; the remaining composite parts would make up 10-15 percent of the airframe: the empennage.
cards.imageCredit: CHIYODA I, CC BY-SA 4.0 via Wikimedia Commons

cards.name: Boeing 737 MAX
cards.subtitle: Boeing · first flew 2016
cards.description: The Boeing 737 MAX is a series of narrow-body aircraft developed by Boeing Commercial Airplanes as the fourth generation of the Boeing 737. It succeeds the Boeing 737 Next Generation and incorporates more efficient CFM International LEAP engines, aerodynamic improvements such as split-tip winglets, and structural modifications.
cards.keyFeatures: In mid-2011, one design objective was matching fuel burn of the 737 MAX to that of the Airbus A320neo's 15% fuel-burn advantage. The initial 737 MAX reduction was 10–12%; it was later enhanced to 14.5%.
cards.imageCredit: Mark Harkin, CC BY 2.0 via Wikimedia Commons

cards.name: Embraer E-Jet E2 family
cards.subtitle: Embraer · first flew 2016
cards.description: The Embraer E-Jet E2 family is a series of four-abreast narrow-body regional jet airliners designed and produced by the Brazilian aircraft manufacturer Embraer. The twinjet is an incremental development of the original E-Jet family, adopting the more fuel-efficient Pratt & Whitney PW1900G, a geared turbofan engine.
cards.keyFeatures: The E-Jet E2 family is based on the first generation E-Jet: its wing is redesigned, and it introduces new pylons, landing gear, horizontal stabilizers, cabin, cabin air system, air cycle machine, bleed air system, and a new fly-by-wire system.
cards.imageCredit: Alan Edwards from Chessington, UK, CC BY-SA 2.0 via Wikimedia Commons

cards.name: Comac C919
cards.subtitle: Comac · first flew 2017
cards.description: The Comac C919 is a narrow-body airliner developed by Chinese state owned aircraft manufacturer Comac. The development program was launched in 2008 as a competitor to the Airbus A320 and Boeing 737. Production began in December 2011, with the first prototype being rolled out on 2 November 2015; the maiden flight took place on 5 May 2017.
cards.keyFeatures: The 2008 program launch initially targeted a maiden flight in 2014. Comac applied for a type certificate for the aircraft from the Civil Aviation Authority of China on 28 October 2010.
cards.imageCredit: Weimeng at www.airliners.net, CC BY-SA 4.0 via Wikimedia Commons

cards.name: Yakovlev MC-21
cards.subtitle: Irkutsk Aviation Plant · first flew 2017
cards.description: The Yakovlev MC-21 (until June 2026: also known as Irkut MC-21, Russian: Яковлев МС-21 / Ирку́т МС-21) is a single-aisle airliner, fully developed in Russia by the Yakovlev Corporation (formerly known as Irkut Corporation), a branch of the United Aircraft Corporation (UAC), itself a 92%-owned subsidiary of Russia's state-owned aviation giant Rostec. The aircraft made its maiden flight on 28 May 2017 from Irkutsk.
cards.keyFeatures: The design is based on the never-released, twin-engine Yakovlev Yak-242 as a development of the three-engine Yakovlev Yak-42.
cards.imageCredit: Dmitry Terekhov from Odintsovo, Russian Federation, CC BY-SA 2.0 via Wikimedia Commons

cards.name: Airbus BelugaXL
cards.subtitle: Airbus Commercial Aircraft · first flew 2018
cards.description: The Airbus A330-743L BelugaXL is a large transport aircraft based on the Airbus A330-200 built by Airbus. The aircraft made its first flight on 19 July 2018, and received its type certification on 13 November 2019. The BelugaXL entered service with Airbus Transport on 9 January 2020.
cards.keyFeatures: With 30% more capacity than the original BelugaST, the BelugaXL can carry two A350 XWB wings instead of one. Its new fuselage is 6.9 m (23 ft) longer and 1.7 m (5 ft 7 in) wider than the original BelugaST, and it can lift a payload 6 t (5.9 long tons; 6.6 short tons) heavier.
cards.imageCredit: Julien Jeany, CC BY-SA 4.0 via Wikimedia Commons

cards.name: Boeing 777X
cards.subtitle: Boeing · first flew 2020
cards.description: The Boeing 777X is an American long-range, wide-body, twin-engine airliner built by Boeing Commercial Airplanes, undergoing flight testing as of 2026. A substantial development from the original Boeing 777, changes for the 777X include General Electric GE9X engines, composite wings with folding wingtips, greater cabin width and seating capacity, and technologies from the Boeing 787 Dreamliner.
cards.imageCredit: Dan Nevill from Seattle, WA, United States, CC BY 2.0 via Wikimedia Commons
